## Final report

**Material and methods (all done with local sequence analysis, no external databases):**
- Parsed `region.fasta`: single record `region_011`, exactly 3000 bp, 47.9% GC, pure ACGT.
- Six-frame ORF/stop-codon mapping (stop-free stretches ≥150 nt).
- Exhaustive exact-repeat scans: direct repeats (≥11 bp) and inverted repeats (≥10 bp).
- Mismatch-tolerant inverted-repeat search (8-mer seeds + extension, ≤20% mismatch).
- Exhaustive target-site-duplication (TSD) scan over all candidate element boundaries.
- Codon-position (GC1/GC2/GC3) and codon-usage analysis per ORF.

**Results:**

| Feature | Finding |
|---|---|
| Longest ORF | **+ strand, 1152–2174 (1023 nt, 341 aa)**, stop-free — statistically significant ((61/64)³⁴¹ ≈ 7×10⁻⁸) |
| Next genes | − strand 240–1013 (258 aa); − strand 2218–2715 (166 aa); − strand 2694–2999 (102 aa) |
| Exact direct repeats ≥12 bp | **none** |
| Exact inverted repeats ≥13 bp | **none** |
| Best imperfect IR | **19 bp / 4 mismatches: 1128–1147 vs 2303–2323** (next best 18 bp/4 mm, 441–918) |
| TSD at candidate boundaries | none significantly above chance |
| Codon usage, 1152–2174 | GC1 55.7 / GC2 37.2 / **GC3 71.0%**, C-ending codons dominate (CTG, GCC, GAG, ACC, CGC…) |
| Codon usage, flanking gene 240–1013 | GC1 47.7 / GC2 48.1 / **GC3 36.4%**, A/T-ending codons dominate |

**Interpretation:** The region is not a canonical "textbook" IS (no long perfect inverted repeats, no clean TSD), but it does contain a single conspicuous *foreign* segment: an ~1195-bp span, **1128–2323**, bounded by a short degenerate inverted repeat (19 bp, 4 mismatches — the strongest palindromic signal in the whole 3 kb, and exactly a transposable-element-sized spacing), and filled almost end-to-end by one long stop-free ORF (1152–2174, 341 aa) whose codon usage is radically different from the surrounding genes (GC3 71% vs 36%, strongly C-ending codons vs A/T-ending). That pattern — a ~1.2-kb block with degenerate terminal inverted repeats enclosing a single ~1-kb gene with horizontally-acquired codon signature — is the signature of an insertion sequence (transposase) rather than of the flanking host DNA. Confidence is moderate rather than high: the element's terminal repeats are degenerate enough that I cannot name the IS family or verify a target-site duplication from the sequence alone.
